_meta.description: Document-rules config for plaint_partition — suit for partition of joint family / co-owned property
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Vineeta Sharma (2020) coparcenary equality and HSA 2005 framework are non-negotiable.

title: Plaint — Suit for Partition of Joint Family / Co-owned Property
displayName: Plaint for Partition (CPC + Hindu Succession Act)

fields.label: Plaintiff full name
Plaintiff father's / husband's name
Plaintiff age
Plaintiff address
Plaintiff's relationship to family (son / daughter / wife / grandchild / coparcener)
All defendants — names, ages, addresses, relationship (every coparcener/co-sharer must be impleaded)
Nature of property
Common ancestor (full genealogy / family tree)
Schedule of properties to be partitioned (movable + immovable, with boundaries / shares)
Share claimed by plaintiff (fraction)
Basis of share calculation — coparcenary rules / HSA S.6 (2005 amendment) / notional partition
Female coparceners — daughters with equal share post HSA 2005 amendment (Vineeta Sharma)
Whether any earlier partition (oral / written / partial) — particulars
Current possession of each property (jointly / by specific defendants)
Income from joint property and accounting sought
Demand for partition made — date, mode, defendant's response
Defendant's denial / refusal to partition
Any alienations by other coparceners to be set aside / declared not binding on plaintiff's share
Consequential reliefs — accounts, mesne profits, injunction against alienation
Cause of action — demand and refusal dates
Limitation — Art. 110 (12 years) for possession by tenant-in-common; right to partition not generally barred so long as jointness continues
Territorial jurisdiction (S.16-17 CPC where property situate; S.17 if multiple jurisdictions)
Court fee paid (Rs.)
Court fee basis — fixed fee on possession-in-joint (S.7(vi) Court Fees Act in some states); state Schedule applies
Suit valuation
Advocate name
Bar Council enrollment number

verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {plaintiff_name}, son/daughter/wife of {plaintiff_father_name}, aged about {plaintiff_age} years, resident of {plaintiff_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above plaint are true and correct to my personal knowledge / family knowledge, and matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Plaintiff

promptInstructions: Draft a plaint for partition of joint Hindu family / coparcenary / co-owned property under CPC read with Hindu Succession Act, 1956 (post-2005 amendment).
Identify the school applicable — Mitakshara (most of India) or Dayabhaga (West Bengal, Assam). Under Mitakshara, coparcener has share by birth; under Dayabhaga, only on father's death.

POST 2005 HSA AMENDMENT (Section 6 HSA): Daughters become coparceners BY BIRTH in same manner as sons, with same rights and liabilities. Survivorship under Mitakshara is ABOLISHED — devolution is now by intestate / testamentary succession, with notional partition on death.

Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) 9 SCC 1 — landmark: daughter is coparcener by birth, irrespective of whether father was alive on 09.09.2005. Reverses Prakash v. Phulavati (2016) 2 SCC 36 on this point.
Para 1: Plaintiff description and relationship to joint family.
Para 2: Defendants — ALL coparceners and co-sharers must be impleaded. Non-joinder of necessary party is fatal (Order I R.9).
Para 3: Common ancestor and genealogy — provide family tree showing descent from common ancestor (typically 3-4 generations).
Para 4: Nature of property — joint Hindu family / Mitakshara coparcenary / Dayabhaga / ancestral / self-acquired property thrown into common hotchpot / co-owned.
Para 5: Schedule of properties — detailed list with boundaries (for land/buildings), denominations (for shares/securities), valuation each.
Para 6: Plaintiff's share computation — per HSA S.6 and notional partition principles. For daughter: equal share with sons. Wife: under notional partition, takes share equal to son in father's share.
Para 7: For pre-2005 demises or earlier partitions, plead carefully — pre-2005 daughters did not have coparcenary status, but Vineeta Sharma clarifies retrospective conferment.
Para 8: Current possession of each property and who is enjoying income.
Para 9: Demand for partition — under Mitakshara, severance of status occurs on unequivocal demand. Plead specific date and mode.
Para 10: Defendant's refusal / denial.

Para 11: Alienations by other coparceners — under Mitakshara a coparcener can alienate his share but not joint family property without consent (except karta for legal necessity / benefit of estate). Plead any alienations to be declared not binding on plaintiff's share.
Para 12: Cause of action — date of demand and refusal.

Para 13: Limitation — right to partition of joint property does NOT extinguish merely by lapse of time so long as jointness continues. Article 110 (12 years) applies for tenant-in-common's exclusion. State right is subsisting.
Para 14: Jurisdiction — S.16 CPC for immovable property; S.17 if properties in multiple jurisdictions (file in any court having jurisdiction over part).

Para 15: Court fee — state-specific. Generally where plaintiff is in joint constructive possession, fixed fee applies (e.g., Bihar Court Fees Act Sch. II Art. 17(vi); Maharashtra Court Fees Act Art. 4 Sch. II). Where plaintiff dispossessed, ad valorem on plaintiff's share. Refer state Schedule.

Para 16: Prayer for: (i) preliminary decree declaring share; (ii) final decree by metes and bounds via Commissioner; (iii) accounting and mesne profits; (iv) injunction against alienation; (v) lis pendens declaration under S.52 TPA.
Note: partition suit follows TWO stages — preliminary decree (declares shares) and final decree (effects physical partition usually through Court Commissioner).
Stamp duty payable on final partition decree (state-specific Schedule).
Verification and affidavit mandatory.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

filing_checklist: Plaint (original + copies for each defendant + court copy)
Memo of parties — every coparcener / co-sharer impleaded
Affidavit in support of plaint (Order VI R.15(4))
Court fee per state Schedule (fixed if joint possession; ad valorem if exclusion)
Title documents of common ancestor (parent deeds, inheritance records)
Mutation entries / khasra-khatauni for all properties (UP/Bihar/Jharkhand)
Records of right / revenue records / 7/12 extracts (Maharashtra) / RTC (Karnataka)
Will (if any) of common ancestor and its probate status
Earlier partition deed / family arrangement (if any)
Property tax receipts and assessment lists
Application under Order 39 R.1-2 for injunction against alienation
Application under S.52 TPA for lis pendens notice
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: defendants_details must not be empty — every coparcener/co-sharer impleaded
If female coparceners exist, women_coparceners must reflect Vineeta Sharma equal shares
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
key_citations: Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) 9 SCC 1 — Daughters are coparceners by birth, regardless of whether father alive on 09.09.2005
Danamma @ Suman Surpur v. Amar (2018) 3 SCC 343 — Pre-Vineeta Sharma, partial recognition
Prakash v. Phulavati (2016) 2 SCC 36 — Overruled by Vineeta Sharma on retrospectivity
Commissioner of Wealth Tax v. Chander Sen (1986) 3 SCC 567 — Post-1956 self-acquired property of father devolves under S.8, not as coparcenary
Yudhishter v. Ashok Kumar (1987) 1 SCC 204 — Coparcenary in modern times
Uttam v. Saubhag Singh (2016) 4 SCC 68 — Notional partition under S.6 HSA
Arshnoor Singh v. Harpal Kaur (2020) 14 SCC 436 — Ancestral property continues as coparcenary among descendants
